utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Here using the word "referendum."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's Official Gazette. We don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S421A and B respectively. S420-1, the conclusions of the Assembly of the Republic of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the session of January 26, 1992. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence under these exhibit numbers. Then let's go back, 420. And now I have to ask from now on Madam Registrar to assist me with the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is the document dated 19th February 1992, from the executive committee of the SDS party of Bosnia-Herzegovina regarding the standpoints in connection with the referendum delivery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is a document preceding the conclusions we just admitted into evidence. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We cannot locate the document. Sorry. The only objection regarding this document is it's not signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Following our practice, admitted into evidence as S420A and B respectively. 419, Madam Registrar, could you please continue helping me out with the...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S419 is the except of Mr. Pejanovic's book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. 418.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The minutes of the joint session of the chambers of the assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. ERN 03075714.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. S417.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: An article from Oslobodenje, formulation of interests of the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. S416.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Another article --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. S415.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Official Gazette of the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Then we have a problem with S413. My proposal would be to admit the document S413 with the caveat that following the testimony of the expert witness, this is a mixum compositum of articles from 1996 and 2000 not edited under the responsibility of the expert witness, but then S413-1, this would be the actual article from June 1996. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was written in June 1996, and published in the August 1996 issue of magazine Chronicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are speaking about the same document apparently, and it's your testimony that you weren't able to find in this short period of time the article of 2000. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as S413 and 413-1. Then we have J32, "The National Question in Yugoslavia" by Ivo Banac. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence under this exhibit number. I think it's not the time now to go through the other binders. It has to be dealt with in a special way, maybe in the same way as we did it with the Mr. Donia's documents. And therefore once again, the invitation to the parties, please tell us whether you have come to an agreement or not. And that we only have to rule on the remaining disputed issues. Madam Registrar just pointed out that there would be a problem with S414, the Kecmanovic report. I think it's mandatory to have this report, that we can find out, and I took it that the expert witness was himself felt attacked that these articles appeared in part in another document just recently presented in this Court in another case. Any objections to the admission into evidence of S414A and B respectively?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence under these numbers. Anything else to be clarified today?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have a B/C/S copy of this report. The only thing I should say is we're not sure whether it's the original B/C/S that he himself wrote or whether it's a translation that was done by us of the translated B/C/S report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it could help out that Dr. Stakic is able to read this document in its totality. And therefore, I would ask the Prosecution to provide Dr. Stakic with this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll make a copy of it tonight, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The remaining and the most crucial problem for me in the moment is that apparently, we have two different reports. Was it possible for the Defence or the expert witness to find out which is the one -- I know what's tendered, but was it intentionally tendered in this maybe abbreviated version or what is the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did not have an opportunity to compare the actual report that's in front of Dr. Trifkovic with that which was filed. However, it's my understanding, because he uses a different computer system, that it's only a question of pagination. We would be happy with the court officer after these proceedings to take the copy that Dr. Trifkovic has and to go through it line by line. But I think the Court will find that the pagination or the font may be slightly different from that which Dr. Trifkovic produced and that which we ultimately submitted to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think, with respect, it's the pagination that's different. It's the footnotes. The pages are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the footnotes, there were -- in the footnotes, you identified the one misleading footnote as 61, and in the report submitted and admitted, it was 63. So this is a discrepancy, and it has to be resolved. And I only can invite the legal officer together with the Defence and also one representative of the Prosecution to go through this document and then let us know tomorrow which is the version which really the one you are prepared to take the responsibility for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I have the answer right away, Your Honour. I think it is the version that the Defence team has and has passed around. The discrepancy may have been caused by the fact that prior to these proceedings, I had a copy printed out of my laptop that I brought with me and that the file in the laptop may have been slightly different to the file from the desktop from which I produced the final version of the report for the Defence team on February 18th or 19th. This was due to my more or less constant travelling since that time. Had I been given simply a photocopy of the same report that was given to the Court, I am sure the discrepancy would have been avoided. But trying to determine the origin of the discrepancy, I am pretty certain that the version given to the Defence team and passed on to the Court is the right one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Trifkovic, it's your responsibility, and you have signed a report, and we -- you will be held responsible for all parts line by line. And therefore, I believe it's more appropriate that we proceed this way. You check it with the Defence only, and if we don't hear by tomorrow morning through the Defence or the court deputy that you do not agree in part with the document submitted, then we take it that you take the responsibility for the report in its entirety as submitted by the Defence. Can we proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, technically, it should be the one that Dr. Trifkovic actually signed as his report. I don't know whether that's the one he has got there, with 61 for the footnotes, or the one that we've got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's the responsibility for the expert in the moment. He gave us an explanation. And he is prepared to take the responsibility. And therefore, it's for the Defence and for the expert to find out whether something has been added or deleted and thereby not authorised by the expert witness. Anything else on an urgent basis for today? So we expect that General Wilmont will appear tomorrow, 9.00 as scheduled. And as envisaged, please let us try that we make a fair distribution of the time left for us. This is two morning sessions. And the expert witness will no longer be available. And therefore, I don't want yet to impose a time limit, but please be aware that this witness will be only here for two days. And I already asked in the past, Prosecution, what about the plans by the Prosecution for next week, for the period of rebuttal as envisaged? It was agreed that during the period of rebuttal, Chamber witnesses could be introduced, and we would start with Witness PST on Monday. It's not yet finally confirmed whether the next Chamber witness will be available on Wednesday. We'll let you know as soon as possible. But as for the other days of next week, we expect by tomorrow the schedule what is the intention of the Prosecution how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll talk to Mr. Koumjian, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then immediately following the period of rebuttal, of course, it can be answered only then by the Defence. We would appreciate to know as soon as possible what would follow in rejoinder. I can't see any other issues for today. Then I have to thank you, Mr. Trifkovic, for coming to The Hague. This Tribunal is not an ordinary criminal court. In addition to that what is ordinary, in stricto senso of a criminal court, we are under the obligation of Chapter 7 of the charter of the United Nations, and the Charter of the United Nations, no doubt, envisage peace and tolerance, and only as a very personal remark, you are no doubt an absolutely intelligent, highly intelligent person. And it's absolutely your right and if not your duty to criticise, but you should be aware that also words out of context can be used and abused by others as weapons. This concludes your testimony. May I ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 4.51 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of March, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25
